findings:
🔵 [repo-identity-json-escape-control-chars] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `_repo_identity_json_str` escapes only backslash and double quote and folds newlines to spaces, so a common-dir path containing a tab or other control char would yield an invalid manifest JSON member and a newline-bearing path would no longer be bit-identical to Node. Excluded: such paths are pathological for a git common dir, the rails already carry `json_escape`/`_flat_json_escape` with the same class of limitation, and no in-scope fixture can trigger it; follow-up is to reuse the rail's escaper or add `\t`/control-char handling.
🔵 [repo-identity-diag-misattributes-non-repo] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `repo_identity_of` emits the single "git rev-parse --path-format failed … need >= 2.31" line for every failure, including a plain non-repo directory on a modern git, and `repo_identity_resolve_fields` does not silence it, so a `--repo-root` pointing at a non-repo prints a misleading version hint on the rail's stderr. Excluded: spec only requires a named one-line failure with empty stdout (met and tested), the manifest field correctly records `git_rev_parse_failed`, and stderr is not parsed by any consumer; follow-up is to branch the message on `git -C <dir> rev-parse --git-dir` success.
🔵 [manifest-test-detach-cleanup-trap] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `hooks/tests/manifest-repo-identity.test.sh` drives three real rails end to end with no cleanup trap killing children by PID and no explicit detach-off env; it relies on `timeout 60` and the rails running foreground under the stub runner. Excluded: the suite is green on the hand's run, every artifact lands under TEST_TMP/fake HOME, and adding a trap is hardening rather than a correctness fix for this row.
